indication.text: SABRIL is indicated as adjunctive therapy for adult patients with refractory complex partial seizures (CPS) who have inadequately responded to several alternative treatments and for whom the potential benefits outweigh the risk of vision loss; not indicated as a first line agent for complex partial seizures

target_moa.text: Vigabatrin is an irreversible inhibitor of gamma-aminobutyric acid transaminase (GABA-T), the enzyme responsible for metabolism of GABA, resulting in increased CNS levels of the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA

citations.quote: it is believed to be the result of its action as an irreversible inhibitor of \gamma-aminobutyric acid transaminase (GABA-T), the enzyme responsible for the metabolism of the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA.
This action results in increased levels of GABA in the central nervous system.

Vigabatrin is an oral antiepileptic drug with the chemical name (\pm) 4-amino-5-hexenoic acid. It is a racemate consisting of two enantiomers. The molecular formula is \text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{NO}_2 and the molecular weight is 129.16.

key_safety.text: Most serious risk is permanent progressive bilateral concentric visual field constriction in 30 percent or more of patients. Most common adverse reactions (≥5% over placebo) include fatigue (28% SABRIL vs 15% placebo), somnolence (24% vs 10%), nystagmus, tremor (15 (3 g) vs 8 placebo), vision blurred, memory impairment, weight gain and confusional state

citations.quote: - SABRIL causes permanent bilateral concentric visual field constriction in 30 percent or more of patients that ranges in severity from mild to severe, including tunnel vision to within 10 degrees of visual fixation, and can result in disability. In some cases, SABRIL also can damage the central retina and may decrease visual acuity.

Most common adverse reactions (change of ≥5% over placebo) in addition to permanent vision loss in adult controlled trials with vigabatrin were fatigue, somnolence, nystagmus, tremor, vision blurred, memory impairment, weight gain, arthralgia, abnormal coordination, and confusional state (6.1)

Pooled data from two SABRIL controlled trials demonstrated that 24% (54/222) of SABRIL patients experienced somnolence compared to 10% (14/135) of placebo patients. In those same studies, 28% of SABRIL patients experienced fatigue compared to 15% (20/135) of placebo patients.

detail.text: WARNING: VISION LOSS — SABRIL causes progressive and permanent bilateral concentric visual field constriction in a high percentage of patients; risk increases with total dose and duration, but no exposure is known that is free of risk of vision loss

citations.quote:
## **WARNING: VISION LOSS**
## See full prescribing information for complete boxed warning
- SABRIL causes progressive and permanent bilateral concentric visual field constriction in a high percentage of patients. In some cases, SABRIL may also reduce visual acuity.

detail.text: A REMS was required, consisting of a Medication Guide, communication plan, and elements to assure safe use; SABRIL is available only through a special restricted distribution program (SHARE)

citations.quote: In accordance with section 505-1 of FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Sabril (vigabatrin) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks of vision loss and of suicidal thoughts and behaviors.
Because of the risk of permanent vision loss, SABRIL is available only through a special restricted distribution program called SHARE, by calling 1-888-45-SHARE.

vote.text: An Advisory Committee was convened on 1/7/09 and 1/8/09; for CPS no formal vote was taken but the committee agreed SABRIL should be reserved for patients refractory to several anticonvulsants and available only under restricted conditions

citations.quote: In order to obtain additional input from the Neurologic community the division convened an Advisory Committee on 1/7/09 and 1/8/09 with experts in adult and pediatric epilepsy as well as ophthalmology.
The committee agreed that Sabril (vigabatrin) should be reserved for patients with complex partial seizures who are refractory to good trials of several anticonvulsants. (No formal vote taken.)
